data.one_liner: Dart SMB2/3 client built on libsmb2 for listings, streaming, downloads, uploads, and watches.
data.what_it_does: Connects to SMB2 and SMB3 file shares on Samba, Windows, and NAS devices. Runs worker isolates for connection pooling, supporting file listings, streaming reads/writes, atomic downloads and uploads, copies, and directory watches across multiple platforms.
use_when: You need to interact with SMB2/SMB3 file shares or NAS devices from a Dart or Flutter application.
You require robust file management operations like recursive directory listings, streaming, and progress-tracked downloads/uploads.
You want network operations to run off the main UI isolate using connection pools.
avoid_when: You only need local device file system access (use standard Dart io instead).
Your target platform is not supported by the underlying libsmb2 native library.
strengths: Pure Dart client with background worker isolates ensuring the UI isolate never waits on the network.
Comprehensive SMB feature set including directory watches, hard/symbolic links, and recursive tree operations.
Built-in automatic reconnection handling and typed SMB exceptions.
weaknesses: Relies on native libsmb2 and OpenSSL dependencies bundled via a build hook, adding significantly to binary size.
Requires strict matching of native library versions if configured through custom user defines.
data.setup_notes: Requires INTERNET permission on Android and network client entitlements on macOS.
